metadata.description: Key Legislative Decrees from the French Mandate period (1920-1943) and early independence period. This is a template for the ~2,000+ decrees from this era.
metadata.notes: The French Mandate period (1920-1943) produced thousands of decrees (Arrêtés) issued by the French High Commissioner that form the foundation of the Lebanese legal system. Many remain in force today. This file captures the most significant ones. A full cataloguing requires access to the Official Gazette archives from 1920-1943.

laws.historical_context: Trademark registration and protection system. One of the oldest still-enforced laws.
Modern property registration (Torrens) system replacing Ottoman land categories.

laws.official_number: Law of March 9, 1932 (Code of Obligations and Contracts)
laws.historical_context: Primary civil law code. See civil_code.json for full entry.
Water rights and concessions. Foundation of Lebanese water law.
Forest protection and management. One of the earliest environmental protection laws.
Governs print media, press freedom, journalist protections, and publication licensing.

laws.official_title_english: Acquisition of Real Property by Foreigners
laws.historical_context: Regulates foreign ownership of real property in Lebanon. Restricts foreign ownership based on area limits and requires prior approval.
First electoral law for the Representative Council. Established confessional seat allocation.
Public accounting and government financial management rules.
Land surveying and cadastral registration system.
Penal code for military offenses and military court jurisdiction.
Established the administrative court system (Conseil d'État / مجلس شورى الدولة).

laws.official_number: Ottoman Nationality Law of 1869 + Arrêté No. 15/S of January 19, 1925
laws.historical_context: Foundation of Lebanese nationality law. Established who qualifies as Lebanese. Controversially, nationality passes primarily through the father (patrilineal system). Decades-long campaign for women to pass nationality to their children has not yet succeeded.
